{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-09-28, as part of the core-identity brainstorm: "probably should review: https://www.omg.org/spec/UAF and the specifications. I'm not saying copy UAF, but more as a way to see if we are missing anything or could improve something." Read the same day: UAF 1.3 (adopted April 2026), Domain Metamodel formal/25-10-01. The comparison is fact:uaf-1-3-read-against-reflow2-2026-09-28.

THE FRAME, from the identity (req:no-se-knowledge: "The graph carries the discipline; the user answers plain questions"). UAF's grid of ten viewpoints by twelve aspects is exactly the expertise a person using reflow2 should never need. So the useful question is not "which UAF views should reflow2 show?" but "which UAF cells should the graph hold, and ask about in plain words, because leaving them empty leaves a design incomplete?"

WHAT THE AUGUST UAF AUDIT ALREADY SETTLED: states, information, materiel and personnel were deferred as a class (dec:the-other-uaf-domains-wait-for-a-project-that-needs-them), to be re-asked when a design needs them. Nothing here reopens that; the trigger stands.

CANDIDATES THE AUGUST AUDIT DID NOT REACH, none chosen:
(a) WHY — UAF's Motivation (drivers, challenges, opportunities, goals, desired effects). reflow2 records a Project objective and business-kind requirements, but has no "why" layer the requirements trace up to. Plain questions: "What's pushing you to build this? What would make it a success? What's in the way?" The gap it would feed: "a requirement no goal needs" and "a goal nothing serves". Small to medium.
(b) WHAT COULD GO WRONG — UAF's Risk (likelihood and consequence of a threat to a capability, goal or asset, mitigated by something). reflow2 has only RISKS/MITIGATES edges between ideas. Plain question: "What could go wrong, how likely is it, and how bad would it be?" This matters most for things that can hurt someone. Medium.
(c) WALK ME THROUGH IT — UAF 1.3's Mission Threads and Phases (an end-to-end sequence of steps to achieve a mission). This is req:scenarios-are-modelled, proposed since July, and UAF confirms its shape. It is the most natural thing a non-engineer can give: the story of a use. Medium; already scoped.
(d) WHO NEEDS TO UNDERSTAND IT — UAF's Stakeholder, Concern and Viewpoint (ISO 42010): a view is chosen by what a stakeholder cares about. reflow2's views slice by aspect, and an open idea asks about altitude (dec:idea-a-view-can-slice-by-altitude-not-only-by-aspect). Plain question: "Who else needs to understand this design, and what do they care about?" The agent then picks and renders the view for that reader. Mostly agent-side. Medium.
(e) HOW WILL YOU KNOW IT'S GOOD ENOUGH — UAF's measurements, required against actual. reflow2 has Constraint limits, budgets and Verification. The weak spot is the other half: no real result has ever been fed back ("loop_closure never_closed"). Small, because the vocabulary exists; the ask is to use it.
(f) LEAVE THE REST TO UAF TOOLS: Security (assets, controls, enclaves), Personnel (competences, posts), and the enterprise scale of Projects and Standards. These are real for defence and enterprise architecture and outside the core identity; this is Alex's "don't do everything".
(g) CHEAPEST OF ALL: QUESTIONS ONLY. Put (a), (b) and (e)'s plain questions into genesis and detect-and-ask, and record the answers as the Requirements, Constraints and Decisions reflow2 already has, with no new vocabulary. It proves whether anyone answers them before any type is added.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
· Every new node type is exactly the growth Alex warns against, and req:functional-vocabulary-computes forbids a type nothing reads. Anything taken must arrive with the detector and the plain question that read it, or not at all.
· UAF is descriptive: it has no notion of what is MISSING, whose word settles intent, drift between design and build, or history. Those are reflow2's distinctive value, and the part to sharpen rather than dilute.
· UAF was built for enterprise and defence architecture. A person designing a greenhouse or a recipe app may need only (b) and (c).
